In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the punch-through particle flux from a 200cm long beam dump, hit by a 30 GeV/ c pion beam, is: (1) for pions, about 1.5×10 −5 pion/cm 2 per beam spill; (2) for K ±, K s and Λ, about 1.3×10 −5 per beam spill, (3) for Ξ, about 0.7×10 −5 /beam spill.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the strange particle flux is reduced by a factor of 2.4 ± 0.4 (stat) ± 0.2 (syst) for the 20 cm increase in length.
the attenuation length of strange particles is not significantly different from that of pions.
the punch-through fluxes from a beam dump are small and that the strange particles are attenuated more effectively than the pions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the attenuation length of strange particles in the beam dump is not much longer than that of pions, which is consistent with a model based on the assumption that the strange particles are produced by pion interactions.
